own_solution.law: a = (m2 - m1) g / (m1 + m2 + M/2) for an Atwood machine with a uniform-disc pulley and no slip.

T1FFD.regime: max string tension (about 38.1 N) < breaking strength

TB3E4.regime: max string tension (about 38.1 N) < breaking strength

defect_reasons.other: The two K variants phrase the limit slightly differently at the exact boundary ('break only above 250 N' vs 'withstand up to 250 N'), a convention at a boundary that no tension reaches (max about 38 N), so it has no effect.

notes: All strata agree with my pass 1. Checks: base a = 2*9.8/9 = 2.17778 (certified 2.17778). R with m1 + q: q = 0.6 -> 1.4*9.8/9.6 = 13.72/9.6 = 1.42917; q = 0.9 -> 1.1*9.8/9.9 = 1.08889; q = 1.3 -> 0.7*9.8/10.3 = 6.86/10.3 = 0.66602. All agree; the right block stays heavier at every listed value, so the direction is unchanged. C: I/r^2 = M/2 for a uniform disc, so the radius cancels; the 'cm' unit does not matter since it cancels. K: tensions T_left = 3*(9.8 + 2.17778) = 35.93 N and T_right = 5*(9.8 - 2.17778) = 38.11 N, both below 150, 250 and 350 N, so every listed value lies in the regime; outside it (e.g. 20 N) the string would break and the blocks would fall freely with a = g, consistent with the reference expression. D rationales are correct: a bench block exerts no force on the system; a block hung and removed before release leaves the stated masses at the start of motion. Minimal pairs: T0DBD/T2D3E share '0.9 kg block' and differ only in attachment (bench vs tied to the left block); TDF61/T30EB differ only in 'taken down again' vs 'left there'. Numeral-free twins TD249 and T3FF0 match their numeric twins with the number replaced. Number consistency across variants holds (0.9 kg, 12 cm, 250 N). Frictionless axle is not stated in the text but is a listed standard idealisation.
